newsitem.title: MEXICO: PEMEX SAYS RECEIVES $1 BLN SYNDICATED CREDIT LINE.
newsitem.headline: PEMEX SAYS RECEIVES $1 BLN SYNDICATED CREDIT LINE.

text.p: Mexican oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Thursday it had been granted a $1 billion syndicated credit line to finance two of its major projects to boost production.
Pemex said in a statement that the line was divided into two tranches, composed of a three-year $625 million credit line and a five-year $375 million credit line.
The credit line will be used to finance exploration and production megaprojects in Cantarell, Mexico's most lucrative crude oil field, and in natural gas rich Burgos Basin, Pemex said.
"This line...is the started point for the financing of projects that are a priority for Pemex," the monopoly said.

Pemex has pledged to spend $5 billion and construct 164 new wells in the Cantarell oil field by 2000 in a move to boost crude output. In the mammoth natural gas drilling project in Burgos, Pemex has pledged to invest about $150 million in 1997 to drill up to 31 wells. The 26 participating banks in the syndicate were led by Chase Manhattan Bank, J.P. Morgan, Citibank, ABN AMRO, Bank of America, Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi, SBC Warburg and UBS, Pemex said.
